simple: A metatable is a hidden settings table you can attach to a normal table to give it special powers. With it, you can decide what happens when someone adds two tables with `+`, reads a key that does not exist, or calls a table like a function. Metatables are an advanced tool, but they power a lot of Roblox code, like making your own object types. This page also covers weak tables and building a set.
analogy: A metatable is like a rule card stuck to the back of a board game box. The box (table) still holds the pieces, but the card says what to do in special situations, like "if a piece is missing, borrow it from this other box".
keyPoints: `setmetatable(t, mt)` attaches metatable `mt` to table `t` and returns `t`. `getmetatable(t)` gets it back.
Metamethods are special keys in the metatable, like `__index`, `__add`, `__call`, and `__tostring`.
`__index` runs when you read a key that is missing. If it is a table, Luau looks the key up there instead.
`__newindex` runs when you set a key that does not exist yet.
Math metamethods like `__add`, `__sub`, and `__div` let you use `+`, `-`, and `/` on tables. Check which side is the table, since `2 / a` and `a / 2` are different.
`rawset(t, key, value)` sets a value without triggering metamethods, which avoids endless loops.
A weak table (using `__mode` set to `"k"`, `"v"`, or `"kv"`) lets the garbage collector remove items nothing else uses.
A set is a collection with no order and no repeats. You can build one with a metatable and add union (`+`) and subtraction (`-`).

terms.metatable: A table attached to another table that holds rules for special actions.
terms.metamethod: A function (or value) inside a metatable that runs when a certain action happens, like `__add` for `+`.
terms.index / indexing: Looking up a key in a table, like `t.x` or `t[1]`.
terms.__index: The metamethod for missing keys. With `__index = { x = 1 }`, reading `t.x` on an empty `t` gives 1.
terms.__newindex: The metamethod that runs when you try to add a new key to the table.
terms.unary minus: The minus sign used on one value to flip its sign, like `-5` or `-myTable`.
terms.concatenation: Joining with `..`. The `__concat` metamethod controls what `..` does with your table.
terms.rawset: Sets a table value directly, skipping `__newindex` and other metamethods.
terms.stack overflow: An error when a function keeps calling itself so many times the computer runs out of room.
terms.strong reference: A normal variable pointing to an object. It keeps the object from being cleaned up.
terms.weak table: A table whose keys or values do not keep objects alive. If nothing else points to them, they can be removed.
terms.garbage collection: Luau automatically deleting things no script can reach anymore. You cannot know exactly when it happens.
terms.set: A group of items with no order and no duplicates. "Apple" is either in the set or not.
terms.intersection / union: Intersection is items in both sets. Union is everything from both sets combined, without repeats.
terms.scalar: A plain single number, as opposed to a vector with several numbers.

example.title: Default stats and adding two points
example.code:
-- 1. Default values with __index
local defaults = { speed = 16, jump = 50 }
local playerStats = setmetatable({ speed = 24 }, { __index = defaults })
print(playerStats.speed) --> 24 (its own value)
print(playerStats.jump)  --> 50 (missing, so it comes from defaults)

-- 2. Make + and tostring work on a custom Point type
local Point = {}
Point.__index = Point

function Point.new(x, y)
	return setmetatable({ x = x, y = y }, Point)
end

Point.__add = function(a, b)
	return Point.new(a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y)
end

Point.__tostring = function(p)
	return `({p.x}, {p.y})`
end

local a = Point.new(1, 2)
local b = Point.new(10, 20)
print(tostring(a + b)) --> (11, 22)
explain: `playerStats` only has `speed`. Its metatable's `__index` points at `defaults`.
Reading `playerStats.jump` finds nothing, so Luau checks `defaults` and returns 50.
`Point` is used as the metatable for every point, and `Point.__index = Point` lets points find shared functions.
`__add` tells Luau how to do `a + b` for points: add the x values and the y values.
`__tostring` decides how a point looks as text, so the result prints as (11, 22).

watchOut: Setting values inside `__index` when `__newindex` blocks them. That loops forever; use `rawset` instead.
Using a weak table to check if a part still exists. Luau can drop the reference while the part is alive; use `AncestryChanged` instead.
Expecting `__eq` to compare a table with any random table. Both must share the same metamethod.
Assuming the table is always the first argument in math metamethods. In `2 / a`, the number comes first.
